ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, it is known that $AB=AD$, $AE=AC=BC$, $\angle 1=\angle 2$, $\angle C=40^\circ$. What is the measure of $\angle ADE$ in degrees?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Since $\angle 1=\angle 2$,\\
it follows that $\angle 1+\angle DAC=\angle 2+\angle DAC$,\\
which means $\angle BAC=\angle DAE$,\\
In $\triangle ABC$ and $\triangle ADE$,\\
since $\left\{\begin{array}{l}AB=AD\\ \angle BAC=\angle DAE\\ AC=AE\end{array}\right.$,\\
it follows that $\triangle ABC\cong \triangle ADE$ (SAS),\\
hence $\angle C=\angle E=40^\circ$, $AE=BC=DE$,\\
therefore $\angle ADE=\angle EAD=\frac{1}{2}\left(180^\circ-\angle E\right)=\frac{1}{2}\left(180^\circ-40^\circ\right)=\boxed{70^\circ}$.

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure, A is upper-left, E is upper-right, and AE is the upper horizontal line segment; B is lower-left, C is lower-right, and D is lower and toward the middle. Line segments AB, BC, and AC form triangle ABC, and line segments AD, DE, and AE form triangle ADE, with AC and DE intersecting in the figure. At point A, angle label 1 is visible between AB and AD, and angle label 2 is between AC and AE; therefore, from the figure, ∠BAC is composed of ∠1 and ∠DAC, and ∠DAE is composed of ∠DAC and ∠2. Reasoning: Given ∠1=∠2, so ∠1+∠DAC=∠2+∠DAC, that is, ∠BAC=∠DAE. Compare triangles ABC and ADE: AB=AD, AC=AE, and the included angles ∠BAC=∠DAE, therefore △ABC≅△ADE (SAS). So the corresponding angles ∠AED=∠ACB=40°, and the corresponding sides DE=BC. Also given AE=BC, so DE=AE. Thus in △ADE, AE=DE, the vertex angle ∠AED=40°, and the base angles ∠ADE and ∠EAD are equal, therefore ∠ADE=(180°−40°)/2=70°. Final answer: 70°.
